source.edition: Elementary Topology, Michael C. Gemignani, Second Edition
source.visualReview: Full supplied PDF pages 91, 96, 97 and 98 inspected, including Definition 4, Proposition 4 and Example 10. Native SVG figures were inspected beside cropped source graphics.
source.boundsConvention: sourceBounds is normalized [x,y,width,height] against the full page. Pixel rectangles include all figure labels and graphics and exclude captions/prose.

implementation.semantics: Immutable shape-free Substance snapshots describe relative openness/closedness, the author's separation axioms, chosen neighborhood witnesses and the infinite deleted-reciprocal topology.
implementation.styleReuse: separationAxiomStyle handles both generic set pairs and point/closed-set pairs. closureNeighborhoodStyle and deletedReciprocalStyle share topologyDrawing and the same label/palette policy. Each policy renders one construction per assembly.
implementation.graphics: Native Penrose PathData, clipped vector hatch groups, circles, lines and equations; no raster wrappers.
implementation.interactive: All four factory functions accept FigureRenderOptions and spread it last. Canonical defaults retain fixed seeds and static source geometry; optional native label interaction is supported.

verification.formatting: Prettier applied to new source and test files
verification.visualReview: All four final SVGs optimized and rendered, rasterized on white backgrounds and compared side by side with source crops. Default canvas framing now matches each inspected source rectangle.
verification.scope: Mathematical relations, constructive numeric overlap invariants, native path-hole rendering and actual optional interactive factory support are checked. Formal universal proofs and pixel-level equivalence are not claimed.

figures.sourceContext: Chapter 5 introduction: disjoint subsets A,B of a specified type can be contained in disjoint subsets U,V, generally open. This graphic is generic and does not state that A or B are closed.
geometry: Two disjoint irregular open supersets U and V, with hatched A and B in their respective interiors.
The original A,B,U,V labels and unequal blob proportions are retained. No point markers or extra arrows are added.
facts: A and B are generic Set objects; neither is assigned ClosedSet.
SetSeparation(A,B,U,V,tau), Subset(A,U), Subset(B,V), Disjoint(A,B), Disjoint(U,V), and relative OpenIn facts.
All contour coordinates and hatching remain Style data.
checks: The generic snapshot contains no ClosedSet objects.
The two inclusion and disjointness witnesses are present.
One reusable policy renders both native regions without image elements.
Optional factory interaction registers four native draggable labels.
limits: The introductory picture supplies a chosen witness, rather than a proof of a universal separation axiom.
Smooth vector contours approximate the scan; gray hatching is retained with consistent pale orange fill.

figures.sourceContext: Definition 4: the author's T3 separates an outside point x from a closed F by disjoint open U,V with x in U and F contained in V. In this edition Regular additionally requires T1.
geometry: Left irregular V encloses hatched closed F; the small separate neighborhood U encloses the marked x.
Original F,V,U,x labels and panel proportions are retained; no metric radius or coordinate data is introduced.
facts: T3(tau) is declared without T1(tau) or Regular(tau).
PointClosedSetSeparation(x,F,U,V,tau), ClosedIn(F,tau), Outside(x,F), NeighborhoodOf(U,x), Member(x,U), Subset(F,V), Disjoint(U,V).
Generic Point x has no drawing coordinates.
checks: The snapshot explicitly retains the author's distinction between T3 and Regular.
Relative closedness, containment and disjointness are checked before drawing.
The same separationAxiomStyle renders the set-pair and point/closed-set constructions.
limits: This is a declared generic witness in a T3 space, not a numeric metric-space construction.
The point neighborhood follows the original irregular outline rather than asserting that it is a metric ball.

figures.sourceContext: Proposition 4 and its proof are on supplied printed page 98 (PDF 97): for x in U, separate x from X−U using V and W, then V⊆Cl V⊆X−W⊆U. The graphic appears on the preceding printed page 97.
geometry: An irregular hatched W surrounds an unfilled X−W hole; a smaller hatched V with marked x lies inside the hole.
Original X−U, W, X−W, U, V and x labels are retained. No extra Cl V label or outline is added.
Oppositely oriented native path subloops make X−W a true geometric hole in both the fill and hatch mask.
facts: Subset(V,ClV), Subset(ClV,X−W), Subset(X−W,U), Subset(X−U,W), and Disjoint(V,W).
checks: The full proof inclusion chain and complement identities are present.
Actual SVG retains two path subloops for W and its complement hole.
The finite shape does not invent metric coordinates for x or the generic sets.
limits: The outer finite contour is a schematic viewport of generic W; no boundedness of the ambient space or its complement is asserted.
The source does not separately draw Cl V. Its mathematical inclusion is declared while preserving the visible V label.

figures.sourceContext: Example 10: nonzero real points have usual interval neighborhoods; zero has neighborhoods (−p,p) minus F={1/n:n positive integer}. F is closed in this topology, zero lies outside it, and every open U containing F intersects any such neighborhood V of zero. Thus the space is T2 but not the author's T3.
geometry: Original horizontal axis with 0, the long hatched V interval marker, one representative U component, and reciprocal term annotations.

The source has three marked terms beyond V and does not give a numerical axis scale. A continuous monotone piecewise linear style chart preserves this order, symmetric mathematical V, and the source's visibly asymmetric placement of 0.
Default mathematical p=0.27, local term 1/6, and arbitrary local openness radius epsilon=0.018. The style draws 32 representative reciprocal terms and the annotated zero.
facts: DeletedReciprocalTopology and ReciprocalSequenceSet store the infinite mathematical rule through a coefficient, not an array of visible terms.
Relative ClosedIn(F,tau), T2(tau), NotT3(tau), Outside(0,F), and UnseparablePointClosedSet(0,F,tau).
V is the whole (−p,p)\F. U is an arbitrary declared open superset of F, with one guaranteed OpenIntervalNeighborhood I about 1/6 and Subset(I,U).
The chosen real z=(1/6)−min(epsilon/2,((1/6)−(1/7))/2) is asserted in I,U,V and outside F via IntersectionWitness.
checks: Zero is included; strict interval boundaries and 300 named reciprocal terms are excluded from V.
For local epsilon values from 10^-8 through 10, the computed witness remains between adjacent reciprocal terms and inside both open sets.
The style verifies the numeric overlap and source-coordinate order before drawing.
Actual SVG renders vector bands and a finite prefix with no image wrappers.
limits: Only one representative component of the arbitrary U is shown, as in the source. Its ellipse does not assert that all of U is a bounded interval.
Dark reciprocal markers annotate points of F that are excluded from V; they do not assert membership in the hatched neighborhood.
The infinite set descriptor is mathematical. Numeric helpers use finite JavaScript coordinates and safe integer indices and reject unrepresentable witnesses.
The original sequence spacing is schematic. The monotone chart preserves order and neighborhood membership without claiming equal display distances for numerical differences.
